chunks: One of our companions, from Ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Karkhi, who said:

I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'The one performing Tamattu' arrives and has no sacrificial animal with him. Should he fast for as long as it is not obligatory upon him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should be patient until the Day of Sacrifice. If he does not find (one), then he is from those who could not find (one).'

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: The one performing Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.لَمْ يَجِدْ: Could not find/afford (referring to the Hady)
key_terms.هَدْيٌ: Sacrificial animal brought by the pilgrim

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim performing Tamattu' who cannot afford the sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the ruling for a Mutamatti' pilgrim lacking a sacrificial animal, instructing them to observe voluntary fasting until the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr) as a form of expiation. If the animal remains unaffordable by that time, the obligation is lifted, reflecting the Shia principle of ease in worship when the specific condition for the penalty is not met. This ruling underscores the distinction between the obligatory Hady of Tamattu' and the compensatory fasting, emphasizing divine mercy in cases of genuine financial hardship.
